explanation: rootkitscan.txt is the raw output of rkhunter (Rootkit Hunter), overwritten each run by rkhunter.sh's cron-daily job (--cronjob --report-warnings-only) and by install-rkhunter's initial check. Unlike aide_report.txt (a file-integrity diff), this is a warnings-style report covering things like suspicious SUID binaries, hidden processes, known rootkit signatures, and unusual system-account configuration. A clean run produces zero warning lines; any warning present is worth reading in full, since rkhunter's warnings are already pre-filtered to unusual conditions.

metadata.reader: human/dashboard only -- not parsed by any script in this bundle
metadata.verification_role: secondary raw-evidence source for rootkit checks, alongside aide_report.txt -- different tool, different report style, both worth reading independently since one can catch things the other misses

value_meanings.no Warning: lines: Clean -- rkhunter's scan completed with nothing flagged.
value_meanings.SSH/rkhunter config mismatch warning: A configuration inconsistency, not necessarily an active compromise -- e.g. sshd allows root login but rkhunter's own config assumes it doesn't. Worth fixing but lower urgency than a rootkit signature match.
value_meanings.passwordless login warning: Genuinely concerning -- an account with no password is a live attack surface, not just a hygiene issue.
value_meanings.unexpected UID-0 account warning: High severity -- a second UID-0 (root-equivalent) account is a classic backdoor pattern, especially if its name isn't 'root'.

raw_content_examples.label: clean
raw_content_examples.content: No warnings found. System looks clean.
raw_content_examples.note: Representative clean-run message -- rkhunter's actual clean output format varies by version but always has zero 'Warning:' lines.

raw_content_examples.label: warnings found
raw_content_examples.content:
Warning: The SSH and rkhunter configuration options should be the same:
         SSH configuration option 'PermitRootLogin': yes
         rkhunter  configuration option 'ALLOW_SSH_ROOT_USER': no
Warning: Password less login for user 'testuser' is possible
Warning: The following user has UID 0 (root) but their login name is not 'root': admin2
raw_content_examples.note: The CATEGORIES shown here (SSH/rkhunter config mismatch, passwordless account, unexpected UID-0 account) were confirmed present in the actual rootkitscan.txt read during the investigation -- the exact usernames and wording above are a reconstruction of that format, not a verbatim capture. Of the three, the UID-0 'admin2' account is the most severe -- it's a functioning backdoor regardless of how it got there.
